title: Stop Rationing Tokens: Let the Harness Pick the Model — Kimchi by Cast AI
talk_summary: Cast AI presents Kimchi, a coding harness that routes each task to different open/proprietary models based on cost per successful outcome, with scoring and remediation loops. It also wraps long-running agent sessions in remote sandboxes and a shared Kanban-style review surface, stopping at staging for human approval.

takeaways.what_they_do: The harness selects a model per task and optimizes for cost per successful outcome, not just token price; model mix shifts automatically as new models appear.
takeaways.evidence_quote: automated harness that will select the right model for the task at the right time based on the outcome of the task
takeaways.numbers: 2.5x savings vs Claude over 3 months; tokens +1.5x; cost -1.5x (speaker claim)

takeaways.technique: Scored completion gate with remediation loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Long-running tasks are broken into milestones, scored, and only complete at a minimum score; below threshold the agent is sent back to fix and rescore.
takeaways.evidence_quote: artifact is only considered complete once like the output of the scoring is like at least a B
takeaways.numbers: B minimum score; A optional; human in loop every 2-3 hours

takeaways.technique: Shared Kanban for agent sessions and plans
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent sessions and plans are visible in a shared board with backlog/in-progress/review states; teammates can claim review questions and answer them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: share your tasks on work in progress and plans which are made by the Kimchi code harness

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent environments run in managed remote containers, continue after the laptop closes, and notify humans only when clarification is needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It spins up sandbox in the remote environment. It's a secure sandbox where you don't need to care about anything.
takeaways.numbers: 62% of engineers use Teleport when coding

takeaways.what_they_do: After a change, the harness runs a build, detects breakage, sends the agent back to fix, rebuilds, and only deploys to staging when clean.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it runs a build for you, it checks if something broke, if something broke, it will go back, do the change again, rebuild again

takeaways.technique: Review intent and spec, not only diff
takeaways.what_they_do: Because agent changesets are large, review compares the diff against the original intent/specification rather than only reading line changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to actually review not just the differences but the actual intent which he wanted to achieve and the specifications
